title: Accessibility of infinity-categorical pullbacks
statement: Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the accessibility and presentability conventions of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. A functor is accessible when it preserves $\kappa$-filtered colimits for some regular cardinal $\kappa$. If $\mathcal A\to\mathcal C\leftarrow\mathcal B$ is a pair of accessible functors between accessible infinity categories, its homotopy pullback $\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal B$ is accessible. The infinity category $\mathcal S$ of small spaces is presentable. Every presentable infinity category admits all small limits as well as all small colimits.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.6.6 (accessible fiber products), Example 5.5.1.8 (spaces), Corollary 5.5.2.4 (limits). No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Write the cospan as $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C\leftarrow\mathcal B:G$ and its homotopy pullback as $\mathcal P$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-compact-approximation] to the finite family of these three categories and two functors. Obtain common cardinals $\kappa<\tau$, with $\tau$ uncountable, such that all three categories are $\tau$-accessible and both functors preserve $\tau$-filtered colimits and $\tau$-compact objects. The same node gives small mapping spaces and essentially small full subcategories $\mathcal A^\tau,\mathcal B^\tau,\mathcal C^\tau$. Let $\mathcal D\subseteq\mathcal P$ consist of triples $(a,b,e)$ with $a,b$ $\tau$-compact; their common image is $\tau$-compact by the chosen functors. The mapping-space description of [lem-coef-accessible-pullback-filtered-colimit] shows that $\mathcal P$ is locally small, since a homotopy pullback of small spaces is small. Since $F(\mathcal A^\tau)\subseteq\mathcal C^\tau$ and $G(\mathcal B^\tau)\subseteq\mathcal C^\tau$, $\mathcal D$ is the full subcategory of triples with components in $\mathcal A^\tau,\mathcal B^\tau$. The full-subcategory clause of [lem-coef-accessible-pullback-filtered-colimit], applied to $\mathcal A^\tau,\mathcal B^\tau,\mathcal C^\tau$, identifies $\mathcal D$ with $\mathcal A^\tau\times^h_{\mathcal C^\tau}\mathcal B^\tau$. Since the three categories are essentially small, the same clause shows that $\mathcal D$ is essentially small. A small set of equivalence classes of objects alone would not prove this; an equivalence to a small quasicategory is required.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.6.6, first paragraph and choice of the compact-object subcategory

proof.text: The colimit and compactness assertions of [lem-coef-accessible-pullback-filtered-colimit], with $\lambda=\tau$, imply that $\mathcal P$ admits small $\tau$-filtered colimits and that every object of $\mathcal D$ is $\tau$-compact. All three component compactness hypotheses are available from Step 1, including compactness of $F(a)\simeq G(b)$ in $\mathcal C$; compactness of the two outside components alone is not being used.

Fix $x=(a,b,e)\in\mathcal P$, and put $c=F(a)$, identifying $G(b)$ with $c$ by $e$. The slice description of [lem-coef-accessible-pullback-filtered-colimit] identifies $\mathcal D_{/x}$ with $K_{\mathcal A}(a)\times^h_{K_{\mathcal C}(c)}K_{\mathcal B}(b)$. Each $K$ is the essentially small compact-source slice of [lem-coef-infinity-compact-approximation]. That node says precisely that the three slices are $\tau$-filtered, admit $\tau$-small $\kappa$-filtered colimits, and that the two maps preserve those colimits and are $\kappa$-cofinal. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-filtered-cofinal-pullback] with these hypotheses: $\mathcal D_{/x}$ is $\tau$-filtered, and both projections are $\kappa$-cofinal, hence cofinal. All these categories are essentially small, so replace them by small equivalent models when taking colimits. The canonical source diagrams from $K_{\mathcal A}(a)$ and $K_{\mathcal B}(b)$ have colimits $a,b$ by the approximation node. The cofinal-restriction assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-filtered-cofinal-pullback] therefore makes the two component diagrams from $\mathcal D_{/x}$ have those same colimit cocones. The componentwise colimit criterion now shows that the canonical diagram $\mathcal D_{/x}\to\mathcal P$ has colimit $x$.

Steps 1-3 exhibit a small collection of $\tau$-compact objects of $\mathcal P$ which generates every object under small $\tau$-filtered colimits. Together with the colimit existence in Step 2 this is the definition of accessibility in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Hence $\mathcal P$ is accessible. This conclusion does not assert that $\mathcal P$ has arbitrary small colimits.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.6.6, conclusion using the compact-generator characterization of accessibility

proof.text: Take the small ordinary terminal category $1$. By [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion], $\operatorname{Fun}(N(1)^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ has small mapping spaces and all small colimits; evaluation at its unique vertex is an isomorphism of simplicial sets onto $\mathcal S$. Choose an uncountable regular $\kappa$ in the small universe using [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] on the singleton family consisting of $\mathbf N$. The point is $\kappa$-compact. Indeed, apply [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density] with $C=\Delta^0$: the representable $h_*$ is the point, since the mapping space of $\Delta^0$ has one simplex in each degree. Under evaluation that node gives a coherent natural equivalence from $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(*,-)$ to the identity functor of $\mathcal S$, which preserves every colimit. A coherent natural equivalence of functors into spaces carries colimiting cocones to colimiting cocones: by the mapping-space colimit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], natural in the diagrams, the two comparison maps differ by homotopy equivalences. The universe-change assertion of [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe] ensures that the resulting small colimiting cocones remain colimiting in the larger space universe used in the compactness definition.

source.place: Example 5.5.1.8, using the point case of the presheaf free-cocompletion theorem and the regular-cardinal choice.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal S$ be the full replete subcategory generated by the point. It is essentially small by [lem-coef-infinity-small-full-subcategory], applied to the singleton family and the locally small $\mathcal S$. By [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density] with $C=\Delta^0$, every space $X$ has a small coherent colimit presentation $p:E_X\to\mathcal S$ by points, hence by objects of $\mathcal G$. Apply the bounded-colimit clause of [lem-coef-locally-small-infinity-size-calculus] to $\mathcal G$ and $\beta=\kappa$. It states that the full replete subcategory $\mathcal D$ of apices of $\kappa$-small colimits of objects in $\mathcal G$ is essentially small; no presentability of $\mathcal S$ is assumed in that size lemma.

source.place: Example 5.5.1.8 and Proposition 5.4.2.9, bounded compact-object family argument via the existing size-calculus node.

proof.text: First, an object equivalent to the apex of a colimiting cocone is itself such an apex. Let $\lambda:p\to\Delta_Kc$ be a colimiting cocone on a coherent diagram $p:K\to\mathcal S$ with $K$ small, and $w:c\to x$ an equivalence edge. Fill the inner horn formed by $\lambda$ and $\Delta_Kw$ in the infinity category $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S)$ to get a cocone $\lambda':p\to\Delta_Kx$ and a $2$-simplex exhibiting it as their composite. By the dual mapping-space criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], natural in the cocone and the test object $y$, the comparison $\operatorname{Map}(x,y)\to\lim_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(p(k),y)$ of $\lambda'$ is homotopic to that of $\lambda$ precomposed with $w^*:\operatorname{Map}(x,y)\to\operatorname{Map}(c,y)$. Since $w$ has invertible component class, the homotopy associativity and unitality in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] make precomposition with an inverse edge a homotopy inverse of $w^*$. Hence $\lambda'$ is colimiting. The identity cocone on the one-vertex diagram at the point is colimiting, its comparison maps being identities. So every $g\in\mathcal G$ is the apex of a colimiting cocone on that diagram, whose vertex value is $\kappa$-compact by Step 5; [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits] makes $g$ $\kappa$-compact. Every object of $\mathcal D$ is likewise the apex of a colimiting cocone on a $\kappa$-small diagram in $\mathcal G$, whose vertex values are now $\kappa$-compact, so the same node makes all of $\mathcal D$ $\kappa$-compact, including the empty colimit. For each $\kappa$-small simplicial subset $L\subseteq E_X$ choose a colimiting cocone for $p|_L$, which exists by Step 5; its apex $q_L$ lies in $\mathcal D$.

source.place: Example 5.5.1.8 and Corollary 5.3.4.15; compactness of apices of small colimits, with apices transported along equivalences.

proof.text: The specified cocones on the $\kappa$-small subdiagrams are assembled by [lem-coef-colimit-subdiagram-approximation] into a small $\kappa$-filtered diagram with values in $\mathcal D$ and colimit $X$. Thus every space is a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit of objects of the essentially small full subcategory $\mathcal D$ of $\kappa$-compact objects. Together with the colimits and local smallness from Step 5, these are exactly accessibility and presentability in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category].

source.place: Example 5.5.1.8 and Proposition 5.4.2.9, compact generation and presentability characterization.

proof.text:
Let $\mathcal E$ be any presentable infinity category and $p:J\to\mathcal E$ a small coherent diagram. The pointwise-limit assertion in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] constructs the actual presheaf $H=\lim_{j\in J}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(-,p(j))$; its values are small spaces, even though $\mathcal E$ may be large. For any small $q:K\to\mathcal E$ with colimit $c$, the contravariant-representable assertion in that same node gives
$$H(c)\simeq\lim_{j\in J}\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(q(k),p(j))\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}H(q(k)).$$
The second equivalence interchanges small limits: a cone to either iterated limit is exactly a compatible family indexed by $J\times K^{\mathrm{op}}$. These are the maps induced by the colimit cocone. Thus $H$ satisfies [lem-coef-infinity-continuous-presheaf-representability], including the empty colimit, and is represented by an object $l\in\mathcal E$. The projections of the pointwise limit $H$ give a coherent presheaf cone. Full faithfulness of Yoneda in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] lifts this cone to $l\to p$. The mapping-space cone criterion of that node makes it limiting, since $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,l)\simeq H(x)$ is exactly the required limit for every $x$. This constructs all small limits, including $J=\varnothing$. All small colimits are part of the definition in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category].

source.place: Corollary 5.5.2.4, proved via the representability criterion and infinity Yoneda
